title: Dandruff that won't quit: a prescription through your AI

Getting medical care for persistent scalp flaking usually means waiting an average of 36.5 days for a new-patient dermatology appointment across 15 metro areas in[AMN Healthcare's 2025 survey](https://ir.amnhealthcare.com/2025-05-27-New-Survey-Shows-Physician-Appointment-Wait-Times-Surge-19-Since-2022,-48-Since-2004) , or joining an online[subscription](https://futureclinic.com/blog/telehealth-subscriptions-vs-paying-a-doctor-per-visit-yearly-cost) that bundles specific products.

## Why having the same doctor matters when dandruff is seborrheic dermatitis


The[American Academy of Dermatology (AAD)](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/a-z/seborrheic-dermatitis-overview) notes dandruff may be the mildest form of seborrheic dermatitis. Both cause itchy, white to yellowish, dry or greasy scale, while seborrheic dermatitis adds inflammation on the scalp, eyebrows, ears, beard, nose creases, or chest. On darker skin, patches can look pink, purple, or lighter, and early care helps prevent dark spots. Per the[AAD](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/a-z/seborrheic-dermatitis-causes) and[MedlinePlus](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000963.htm) , it is not contagious, not an allergy, and not from unclean skin; a reaction to *Malassezia* yeast fed by skin oil likely drives flares.


Because flares return in cold, dry winter weather or stress, messaging the same doctor time after time lets you build trust, try treatments together, and track progress, swapping a drying wash for a scalp oil or stepping down from a short steroid course to weekly maintenance.


## Why drugstore shampoos stop working and what to try first


Over-the-counter washes under the[US OTC monograph (21 CFR 358.710, as it stood in March 2020)](https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2020-03-01/title-21.xml?part=358&section=358.710) or FDA approval use pyrithione zinc (0.3% to 2%),[selenium sulfide 1%](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=selenium) , salicylic acid (1.8% to 3%), sulfur (2% to 5%), coal tar (0.5% to 5%), or[ketoconazole 1% shampoo](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=ketoconazole) (Nizoral, ages 12+). The[AAD advises](https://www.aad.org/public/everyday-care/hair-scalp-care/scalp/treat-dandruff) leaving washes on 5 to 10 minutes when directed, rotating ingredients, and matching the routine to hair type: wash daily and use dandruff shampoo twice weekly for fine, straight, or oily hair, or apply it to the scalp once weekly for coarse, curly, or coily hair. If ketoconazole 1% fails after 2 to 4 weeks, its label says to ask a doctor, who can distinguish seborrheic dermatitis from psoriasis, eczema, or fungal infection.


## AI dandruff treatment: what a doctor can prescribe by message


A[2026 European consensus of 33 specialists](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42012301/) favors combining antifungal and anti-inflammatory care. If your doctor decides it's right for you after reviewing your history and photos, they can send[prescriptions](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/a-z/seborrheic-dermatitis-treatment) to the pharmacy you choose, including mail-order pharmacies that deliver to your door:


-


**Antifungal washes and creams:**[Ciclopirox 1% shampoo](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=ciclopirox) (FDA-approved for adults, twice weekly for 4 weeks) gave effective treatment in 58% and 26% of trial patients at week 4 versus 31% and 13% on vehicle.[Selenium sulfide 2.5% lotion](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=selenium) is approved for dandruff and scalp seborrheic dermatitis. Doctors also prescribe ketoconazole 2% shampoo off-label, and FDA-approved ketoconazole 2% cream or foam (ages 12+). In a[2015 Cochrane review of 51 trials](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25933684/) (9,052 people), ketoconazole 2% cut failed clearance by 31% at 4 weeks versus placebo and matched steroids with 44% fewer side effects. On[Cost Plus Drugs](https://api.costplusdrugs.com/pricelist/cpd) as of October 2026, 120 mL of ketoconazole 2% shampoo is $11.75 ($17.00 with shipping), selenium sulfide 2.5% lotion is $17.64 ($22.89 shipped), ciclopirox 1% shampoo is $27.60 ($32.85 shipped), and ketoconazole 2% cream (30 g) is $8.75 ($14.00 shipped).


-


**Topical corticosteroids:** A[2014 Cochrane review of 36 trials](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24838779/) (2,706 people) found topical steroids effective for scalp and face flares, with mild steroids matching strong ones short term. Cost Plus Drugs prices as of October 2026 include[fluocinolone 0.01% solution](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=fluocinolone) ($8.16 for 60 mL, $13.41 shipped), fluocinolone 0.01% scalp oil ($16.67 for 118.28 mL, $21.92 shipped), and[clobetasol 0.05% shampoo](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=clobetasol) ($11.59 for 118 mL, $16.84 shipped, off-label).


-


**Steroid-free options:** Doctors may prescribe tacrolimus ointment or pimecrolimus cream off-label, short term, for people with a healthy immune system, or[roflumilast 0.3% foam (Zoryve)](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=roflumilast) , FDA-approved for seborrheic dermatitis from age 9, once daily (the AAD says it can go on any affected skin, including the scalp, nose, eyebrows, ears and eyelids), which is contraindicated in moderate to severe liver impairment. In Zoryve trials, 79.5% and 73.1% of patients were clear or almost clear at week 8 versus 58.0% and 40.8% on vehicle.[GoodRx](https://www.goodrx.com/zoryve) lists Zoryve 0.3% foam (60 g) at $939.62 (average retail $1,132.95) as of October 2026; when insurance needs a prior authorization, FutureClinic helps get it.


For a stable medicine, your doctor can prescribe several months at once when they judge it safe, with a discount coupon for the best cash price. FutureClinic doctors do not prescribe controlled medicines.
